findings.claim: The new `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys skips the rest of the member's loop body. That includes the `[MessagePackFormatter]` attribute handling (visible right after the key branches) and any later collection or validation of `item.Type`. So a member whose key kind mismatches no longer gets diagnostics about its formatter attribute or member type, such as an invalid formatter type or problems in a type reachable only through this member. These appear only after the user fixes the mixed-key error. Base threw at `intKey!.Value` here, so this is fewer diagnostics rather than a regression from working behaviour, and MsgPack's mixed-key rule is an Error anyway.

receipt_plan.detail: Read TypeCollector.cs:1005-1060 and 1145-1195. The `continue` at 1008/1148 bypasses the `messagePackFormatter` lookup at ~1045/~1185 and the per-member type collection that follows. Example input: [MessagePackObject] class C { [Key(0)] public int A {get;set;} [Key("b"), MessagePackFormatter(typeof(NotAFormatter))] public int B {get;set;} }. Only the mixed-key diagnostic is reported for B; the formatter-related diagnostic is not.
